requirements.description: Ask and stream: the owner submits a shopping question and sees ordered research progress until exactly one terminal state.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat streams data-progress parts in the order candidates, offers, validate, compare.
Each run ends in exactly one of completed, failed, or cancelled.
The UI shows the current stage, disables input while running, and offers Cancel.

requirements.description: Cited comparison: a completed run shows a comparison of 1-3 candidates whose citation markers resolve to Exa citations from the same run.
acceptanceCriteria: Every rendered source link is a citation URL returned by Exa in this run.
Out-of-range markers are removed and counted; paragraphs with no resolved marker are visibly flagged uncited.
All cases in evals/cases/citations.json and evals/cases/citations-spaced.json produce their expected results, including markers written with spaces such as [2, 5, 6] (CR-001).

(v1.1) Comparison text containing '{' or '}' is cut before the first such character and its citations resolved on the kept text; the UI notes "Exa's answer ended in malformed output, which is not shown."; if no letter remains, the comparison is replaced by that note (D-042, EV-012 comparison cases).

requirements.description: Authentic, relevant merchant offers: only direct, validated merchant product pages for the candidate model are offers; other pages are labeled evidence or rejected; prices are never invented or edited.
acceptanceCriteria: Every displayed offer has merchant host, positive price, supported ISO currency, canonical http(s) URL from this run, availability enum value, source exa, and retrievedAt.
Aggregator, editorial, non-listing, price-less, and merchant-mismatch pages appear only in a separately labeled evidence section.
Irrelevant products, unsupported currencies, URLs not from the run, and non-http URLs never appear as offers.

All 54 cases in evals/cases/offer-classification.json produce their labeled outcome, category, and offer fields, except that L29 and Y03 produce the superseding labels recorded in evals/cases/offer-classification-v1-1.json (D-031, D-032).
(v1.1) Marketplace and search-or-category pages also appear only as labeled evidence (REQ-016).

requirements.description: Currency-safe ranking: offers group by USD, SGD, JPY with the selected market's currency first, sort deterministically within a group, and are never compared across currencies.
acceptanceCriteria: All cases in evals/cases/ranking-currency.json produce the expected groups and order.
A seeded property test over 1,000 generated offer lists shows no mixed-currency group and no lost or duplicated offers beyond the canonical-URL collapse.

requirements.description: Failure recovery: Exa errors and cancellation end the run with a typed, visible reason, partial results are labeled, and live mode never falls back to fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: 401, 402 or credit errors, 429, 5xx, timeout, no candidates, and no offers each yield the specified data-error kind or empty state; a client cancel aborts the Exa call, ends the stream, and shows the client-side cancelled state.
A failure after the candidates stage sets partial true and keeps already validated products visible.
The next question works after any failure.

requirements.description: Spend guard and cache: at most 5 Exa requests per question by construction, at most 3 for a normal question, 6-hour cache, monthly limits, and stop on exhausted credits.
acceptanceCriteria: No sequence of candidates, retries, or errors makes a sixth Exa call in one run.
A repeated question within the TTL makes no Exa call and shows the original retrievedAt.
Monthly request and cost limits block calls before they are made; a 402 or credit error blocks later calls until reset.
Each response's costDollars.total is added to the ledger and shown in the run's usage.
(v1.1) Image fetching never takes a RequestBudget token, never calls Exa, and never writes the Exa ledger.

requirements.description: Local and key safety: the server listens only on 127.0.0.1, rejects foreign Host or Origin, and the Exa key never leaves the server process.
acceptanceCriteria: The listen address is hard-coded to 127.0.0.1; requests with a foreign Host or cross-origin Origin get 403.
A test key string is absent from a production build, server logs, .cache/ (including .cache/images/), evals/fixtures/, API responses, and browser storage.

(v1.1) Every server response except /api/image/:id carries the Content-Security-Policy in docs/futari/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Content-Security-Policy', so the browser loads scripts, styles, images, fonts and API calls only from 127.0.0.1; the Host/Origin guard also covers /api/image/:id.

requirements.description: Live acceptance (v1.1, replaces the MVP's 6-query suite, D-034): the 8-query live suite in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-1.json meets its thresholds within the live usage limits before v1.1 is declared complete.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 6 of 8 queries show at least one merchant offer, and at least 3 of the 4 SG queries show an SGD offer in a card's main list.

At least 12 offers are displayed; 100% pass revalidation against the recorded Exa responses; owner audit failures are at most floor(10% of displayed offers); no search or category page and no fabricated offer is displayed.

At least 6 images are displayed and at least 70% of offer-bearing cards show a loaded image; 100% of displayed images pass revalidation; owner image audit failures are at most max(1, floor(10% of displayed images)).

No displayed comparison or reason contains '{' or '}'; no browser request leaves 127.0.0.1 and no unexpected error run occurs; at most 5 requests per query, 40 per suite run, $0.50 per suite run, 3 suite runs, and the plan-wide cap of 130 requests and $1.50 of reported cost governs.

requirements.description: Persistent local history: the conversation survives reloads through versioned, validated localStorage and can be cleared with confirmation; no secret is stored in the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: After a reload the full conversation, including results, is restored.
Clear history asks for confirmation, then empties the thread and removes kensaku.history.v1.
Invalid stored data is discarded with a visible notice.
(v1.1) The frozen MVP history payload evals/fixtures/history/mvp-history-xm5-sg.json, loaded unchanged, renders as v1.1 product cards with the image fallback and without key-spec or reason sections.

requirements.description: Frontend quality and components: the UI uses unmodified official AI Elements and shadcn/ui components, has a persistent market selector, and meets accessibility, layout, and owner visual review. (v1.1: in both themes, with the image-first cards.)
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-components.mjs confirms every installed component file matches components.lock.json and components.json lists the @ai-elements registry.
axe reports zero serious or critical violations on empty, running, completed, and error states; the journey works by keyboard alone. (v1.1) This holds in the dark and the light theme.
At 375 px width there is no horizontal page scroll.
The owner records visual review of the v1.1 cards on desktop and mobile widths in both themes in .futari/evidence/JM-105.md.
(v1.1) No new design system or hand-edited component is introduced, and the CSS variables in src/web/index.css are unchanged.

requirements.description: Theme: dark is the default for first-time visitors, an accessible toggle in the header switches between dark and light, the choice persists, and the first paint already uses the right theme.
acceptanceCriteria: With no stored preference, the page renders dark regardless of the operating system's prefers-color-scheme.

A header button with an accessible name ('Switch to light theme' or 'Switch to dark theme') toggles the theme by mouse and keyboard and stores 'dark' or 'light' in localStorage kensaku.theme.v1; reloads keep the choice.

The theme class and color-scheme are set by a blocking script before the app bundle runs, so with the bundle delayed the page already shows the chosen theme; an invalid stored value or unavailable localStorage falls back to dark without an error.
Theming uses the shadcn/ui class-based .dark convention and the existing CSS variables in src/web/index.css only.

requirements.description: Image-first product cards: each recommended product gets its own generously sized card with a large image, name, price summary, key specifications, recommendation reason, and merchant offers, with research details available but collapsed.
acceptanceCriteria: At 1280 px viewport width product cards sit two per row, each at least 480 px wide; at 375 px they sit one per row with no horizontal page scroll.

Each card's image is full-bleed: it spans the card's full width (no inner padding) at a 4:3 aspect ratio above the text; at 1280 px it is at least 360 px tall, and at 375 px it is at least 300 px wide (so at least 225 px tall).

A card shows, in order: product name (candidate brand and name), image with caption, price summary ('From <lowest listed price> <code>') from offers in the market's currency only, up to 5 key specifications, the cited recommendation reason, the merchant offer list, an 'Other markets' disclosure when other-currency offers exist, and a 'Research details' disclosure with evidence and rejected counts; the card reads key specs and the reason only from the normalized data-products entry fields, never from the raw candidate.

The product heading names the product, never a merchant; each offer row names its merchant host, merchant name, price with ISO currency code, availability, retrieval time, and a 'View offer' link, so a product with several merchants reads as one product with several offers.

Reason citations render with the AI Elements inline-citation component and resolve under the EV-004 rule after the leaked-structure cut (D-042); the comparison text and its Sources stay above the cards.

requirements.description: Real product images: images come only from the product pages of this run's merchant offers or from the manufacturer's page, under rules I1-I3, with loading states, attribution, and a graceful fallback; nothing is generated or invented.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline selects up to 4 image candidates per product with rules I1 and I2 in evals/cases/image-selection.json, and the proxy accepts bytes only under rule I3; no image ever comes from aggregator, editorial, marketplace, search-or-category, merchant-mismatch, or rejected pages.
The card shows a skeleton while an image loads, tries candidates in order, and shows a 'No verified product image' fallback (no broken-image icon) when none loads.
The caption names the source page's host and its product title as Exa reported it (so a colour variant is named), and the image's alt text is '<brand> <name>, image from <host>'.
No image is generated, edited, or taken from a source outside this run's Exa results.

requirements.description: Image proxy safety and cache: the server fetches and serves only image URLs registered by a research run, blocks private networks, validates bytes, and caches bytes and metadata on disk.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/image/:id serves only ids registered by a run (SHA-256 of the image URL); unknown or malformed ids get 404 without any outbound request; requests whose Sec-Fetch-Site header is present and not same-origin get 403, and every response carries Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin.

Only http and https URLs on ports 80 or 443 are fetched; every connection, including each of at most 3 redirects, goes to an address that was resolved once for that hop and checked: IPv4 must be public unicast and IPv6 must be in 2000::/3 outside 2001::/32, 2001:db8::/32 and 2002::/16; URL hosts that are IP literals are checked the same way. The connection is made with node:http or node:https to the checked address.

Fetches send no cookies, credentials, or Referer, time out after 8 s, stop at 5 MiB, and accept only bytes passing rule I3; responses use the sniffed image type, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'.

Accepted bytes are reused for 7 days and then refetched while the registry entry exists; registry entries are pruned 30 days after their last registration, and bytes are evicted oldest-first above 500 MB in total; rule I3 rejections are cached for 24 hours and upstream failures for 10 minutes; image fetching never uses Exa or the Exa budget.

requirements.description: Market relevance and currency presentation: offer searches name the market, the card's main offer list shows only the selected market's currency, and other currencies are collapsed under 'Other markets'.
acceptanceCriteria: The offer search query is '<brand> <name> price <United States|Singapore|Japan> buy' with userLocation set to the market.

A card's main offer list and price summary use only offers in the market's currency; offers in other supported currencies appear in a collapsed 'Other markets (may not ship to <market name>)' disclosure, and no conversion is ever shown.
When a product has no offer in the market's currency, the main list says 'No <market name> offers found' and the Other markets disclosure stays collapsed.
Prices show the amount with the ISO currency code (for example '289.00 SGD'); symbols such as '$' are never shown alone.
